childhoodSituations.name: Toy not shared or taken away
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I have to react when things feel unfair.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can pause and choose my response.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Hot frustration and a flash of 'that's mine' — wanting to grab it back.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That other people's feelings matter too, even when something feels unfair.

childhoodSituations.name: Screen time cut off suddenly
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I have to get what I want immediately.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can handle disappointment and make wise choices.
childhoodSituations.feeling: A sudden jolt of protest — the fun was cut off with no warning.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That transitions go easier with a heads-up, and endings aren't punishments.

childhoodSituations.name: Told 'no' without explanation
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: If people say "no", they don't care about me.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can listen, ask and understand even when I don't like the answer.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Stubborn defiance — wanting a reason, not just an order.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That some rules don't need debate, and trust can hold even without an explanation.

childhoodSituations.name: Sibling gets bigger portion or more attention
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Someone else's success makes me less important.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Everyone has their own gifts and my worth doesn't depend on comparison.
childhoodSituations.feeling: A sting of unfairness — feeling smaller and less important than a sibling.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That love isn't measured in portions, and being loved doesn't mean being equal.

childhoodSituations.name: Can't finish homework or a craft
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: If I can't do it quickly, I can't do it.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Every attempt helps me improve.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Rising frustration at their own hands not doing what their mind wants.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That struggling is part of learning, not proof they're bad at it.

childhoodSituations.name: Playdate or plan suddenly cancelled
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Plans must happen my way.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can adapt and still enjoy life.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Sharp disappointment — an exciting plan just disappeared.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That plans can change and disappointment can be survived without spoiling everything.

childhoodSituations.name: Someone breaks their Lego or drawing
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: My anger should decide what I do.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can choose calm actions even when I'm upset.
childhoodSituations.feeling: A wave of anger at seeing something they made get destroyed.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That things can be rebuilt, and their effort still counted even if it broke.

childhoodSituations.name: Being hurried to put shoes on or leave
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Everything has to happen right now.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can slow down and work with the moment I'm in.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Irritable resistance to being hurried when they weren't ready.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That slowing down sometimes isn't possible, but their pace still matters.

childhoodSituations.name: Feeling hungry or extremely tired (hangry)
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I can't cope when my body feels uncomfortable.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can care for my body and uncomfortable moments will pass.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Short-fused crankiness that isn't really about what just happened.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That big feelings are sometimes just a full tummy or tired body in disguise.

childhoodSituations.name: Blamed for something they didn't do
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Being blamed means nobody believes me.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can respond honestly and calmly, even when things feel unfair.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Indignation at being punished for something they didn't do.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That being falsely blamed hurts, and it's safe to say so calmly.

childhoodSituations.name: Being teased or physically pushed
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: If someone hurts me, I should hurt them back.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can protect myself without losing control.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Fear tangled with anger — wanting to hit back or hide.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That standing tall doesn't require becoming what hurt them.

childhoodSituations.name: No say in what to wear or eat
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I should always get to decide everything.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can cooperate even when I don't get my way.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Frustration at having no vote in small everyday decisions.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That a little choice, even in small things, builds real self-trust.

childhoodSituations.name: Adult doesn't understand what they mean
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: If people don't understand me, something is wrong with me.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can express myself patiently and be myself.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Helpless irritation at not being understood, even while trying to explain.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That being patient while explaining again is its own kind of strength.

childhoodSituations.name: Game crashes or internet lags during a win
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: One setback ruins everything.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can begin again after setbacks.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Sharp letdown when a win gets erased by something out of their control.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That effort still counts even when the outcome gets taken away.

childhoodSituations.name: Forced to sit still too long (car, flight)
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I can't stay calm when I feel trapped.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can find peaceful ways to handle uncomfortable moments.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Restless, fidgety irritation at a body that wants to move.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That stillness is a skill that grows, not a switch that flips.

childhoodSituations.name: Game save file corrupted or deleted
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Losing my progress means I've failed.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can rebuild and keep moving forward.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Grief-tinged anger at losing hours of effort in an instant.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That things we build can be rebuilt, and the loss still deserves comfort.

childhoodSituations.name: A treat or promise was forgotten
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Broken promises mean people don't care about me.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Trust grows through honesty, reliability and understanding.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Betrayal-flavored disappointment when a promised treat quietly vanishes.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That promises matter, and it's fair to remind grown-ups gently when one slips.

childhoodSituations.name: Sibling tells on them unfairly
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I have to get even when something feels unfair.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can respond with honesty instead of revenge.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Anger at being reported on, especially if it feels exaggerated.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That tattling and telling are different, and both siblings deserve fairness.

childhoodSituations.name: Scratchy clothes or irritating noise
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I can't be okay when things feel uncomfortable.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can stay peaceful even when my surroundings aren't perfect.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Irritable discomfort that has nothing to do with anyone's behavior.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That bodies have limits too, and naming discomfort isn't complaining.

childhoodSituations.name: Repeatedly failing a level or concept
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: If I keep failing, I should quit.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Every challenge helps me become stronger.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Mounting frustration at hitting the same wall again and again.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That repetition isn't failure — it's how mastery actually happens.

childhoodSituations.name: Darkness or shadows in the room
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Fear means I should stop.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Courage is taking one small brave step.
childhoodSituations.feeling: A prickle of dread when the room turns unfamiliar in the dark.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That the dark hides nothing new, just what daylight already showed.

childhoodSituations.name: Thunder, fireworks, or loud sirens
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Loud or unexpected things mean I'm not safe.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can find safety, calm and support.
childhoodSituations.feeling: A full-body startle at a sound too loud to predict.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That loud sounds pass, and their body can learn to settle after the jolt.

childhoodSituations.name: Monsters under the bed or scary stories
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: My imagination can control me.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can be braver than my fears.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Vivid, sticky fear from an imagined creature that feels very real.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That imagination can also invent safety, not just monsters.

childhoodSituations.name: Parent leaving for work or a long trip
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: When someone leaves, they might not come back.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can trust the people who love and care for me.
childhoodSituations.feeling: A tight knot of worry that the goodbye might be a forever one.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That leaving and returning are part of the same promise, kept every time.

childhoodSituations.name: Fear of going on stage or presenting
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: If I'm nervous, I can't do it.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Confidence grows each time I try.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Stomach-churning stage fright — every eye suddenly too much.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That shaky knees and a steady voice can exist in the same moment.

childhoodSituations.name: Anxiety before a big test or result
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: If I don't do well, I'm not good enough.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: My effort and learning matter more than perfect results.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Anticipatory dread that builds for days before the actual test.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That preparation is protection, and one result doesn't define their worth.

childhoodSituations.name: Injections, doctors, or dentist visits
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: If something hurts, I can't handle it.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I am stronger than I think, even during difficult moments.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Sharp anxiety about pain that hasn't even happened yet.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That brief discomfort can be survived, and asking for comfort is allowed.

childhoodSituations.name: New teacher or unfamiliar adult
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: New people won't understand or help me.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Trust grows one step at a time.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Wary uncertainty around someone new whose intentions aren't known yet.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That caution is wise, and warming up slowly is not the same as rudeness.

childhoodSituations.name: Fear of getting lost in a mall or crowd
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: If I'm alone, I'm not safe.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can stay calm, make wise choices and find help.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Panic at the thought of a familiar hand suddenly not being there.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That a plan for 'what if we get separated' turns fear into readiness.

childhoodSituations.name: Accidentally saw a scary or violent video
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: The scary things I see will happen to me.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can separate imagination from reality and seek comfort.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Intrusive, unsettling images that won't easily leave their mind.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That not everything seen online is meant for their eyes, and that's okay to say.

childhoodSituations.name: Heard about war or violence on news
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: The world is always dangerous.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: There are many people working every day to keep others safe.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Heavy, adult-sized dread about something too big to fully picture.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That caring adults are working on big problems, and their job is just to be a kid.

childhoodSituations.name: Saw news about floods, fires, earthquakes
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Bad things mean everything is ruined forever.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: People can help, rebuild and begin again.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Overwhelm at scenes of destruction that feel close even from far away.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That most places, most days, are safe — and helpers exist for the hard days.

childhoodSituations.name: Fear that a parent might get sick
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I might lose the people I love.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Love, care and support help us through uncertain times.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Quiet, private fear they might be carrying alone.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That saying a fear out loud to a trusted adult makes it smaller, not bigger.

childhoodSituations.name: Overheard adults talking about money problems
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: We won't be okay if money is tight.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Families work together and find solutions during hard times.
childhoodSituations.feeling: A confusing unease absorbed from grown-up conversations not meant for them.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That money worries are a grown-up job, and they are still fully provided for.

childhoodSituations.name: Overthinking imaginary future dangers
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I have to believe every scary thought.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Thoughts are not always facts, and I can return to the present.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Spiraling worry about things that haven't happened and may never.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That imagined futures aren't facts, and today is the only place to stand.

childhoodSituations.name: Fear of being laughed at by class
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: If others laugh at me, I don't matter.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: My value isn't decided by other people's opinions.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Sharp social dread — imagining every eye and every laugh.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That embarrassment fades fast, faster than it feels in the moment.

childhoodSituations.name: First day at a new school
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I won't fit in here.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can make connections while being myself.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Nervous unfamiliarity about a place with no known faces yet.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That every friend was once a stranger, and the first day is just the start.

childhoodSituations.name: Fear of dogs, spiders, or insects
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Fear means I should avoid everything unfamiliar.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can learn, stay safe and become braver step by step.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Instinctive alarm at something small, fast, or many-legged.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That fear can be respected without needing to run the whole show.

childhoodSituations.name: Fear of falling or getting hurt at park
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: If I fall once, I shouldn't try again.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Trying again helps me grow stronger and more confident.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Wary caution about a body that sometimes surprises them.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That falling is part of moving, and their body knows more than fear admits.

childhoodSituations.name: Fear of getting in trouble with teacher
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Making mistakes makes me a bad child.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Honesty and responsibility are more important than being perfect.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Anxious dread about disappointing someone with authority.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That mistakes and consequences are both survivable, and trust can hold through both.

childhoodSituations.name: Anxiety about the earth breaking (climate change)
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Nothing I do can make a difference.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Small caring actions can help create a better future.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Diffuse, grown-up-scaled anxiety about a world too large to control.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That small daily actions matter, and worry doesn't have to carry the whole planet.

childhoodSituations.name: Friend is not playing with them today
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: If my friend chooses someone else, I'm not important.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Friendships can grow even when people spend time with others.
childhoodSituations.feeling: A quiet ache of being left out of today's fun.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That one day of distance doesn't undo a friendship.

childhoodSituations.name: Death of a pet
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Love disappears when someone is gone.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Love stays with us through our memories and kindness.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Deep, unfiltered grief for a companion who won't come back.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That loving something means grieving it fully, and grief is love with nowhere to go yet.

childhoodSituations.name: Death of a relative or family member
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Life will never feel happy again.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Love continues through memories, family and hope.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Heavy, disorienting sadness around a loss too big for words.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That missing someone forever is the price and the proof of having loved them.

childhoodSituations.name: Lost a favourite toy or comfort blanket
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I can't be okay without this special thing.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: The love and comfort I feel live inside me too.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Sharp grief over something small to others but precious to them.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That objects can be mourned too, and new comfort can still be found.

childhoodSituations.name: Harshly reprimanded by a parent
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: When I make mistakes, I'm not loved.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can make mistakes and still be deeply loved.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Stinging shame layered under sadness after being scolded hard.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That correction and love can coexist, even when a voice was raised.

childhoodSituations.name: Feeling invisible to a busy parent
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I'm not important because nobody notices me.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I matter even when people are busy.
childhoodSituations.feeling: A lonely ache of not being noticed, even in a full house.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That being busy isn't the same as not caring, and both can be true.

childhoodSituations.name: Not invited to a birthday party
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Being left out means nobody likes me.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: One invitation does not decide my worth or my friendships.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Sharp exclusion — wondering what made them not good enough to invite.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That not every gathering includes everyone, and that isn't a verdict on their worth.

childhoodSituations.name: A fall or scrape — the shock of pain
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Getting hurt means I should stop trying.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can heal, recover and keep growing.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Shock and sting that arrive together in the first seconds of pain.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That comfort matters as much as the injury, and both deserve attention.

childhoodSituations.name: Missing a parent who travels often
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Distance means love becomes smaller.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Love stays strong even when people are far away.
childhoodSituations.feeling: A steady undercurrent of missing someone who's often away.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That distance doesn't shrink love, and counting days can make waiting easier.

childhoodSituations.name: Close friend moved to another city
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: If someone leaves, our friendship is over.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Real friendships can continue across distance and time.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Grief for a friendship that now has geography in the way.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That friendships can stretch across distance, even if they change shape.

childhoodSituations.name: Moving house and leaving familiar bedroom
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Everything familiar is gone forever.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Home is built through love, memories and new beginnings.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Disoriented sadness at losing the small, familiar details of home.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That a new room can become familiar too, in its own time.

childhoodSituations.name: Long illness, lockdown recovery, school break
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Life will never feel normal again.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can adapt and create new routines after change.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Fatigue-laced sadness from days that all started to blur together.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That slow recovery is still progress, even without visible milestones.

childhoodSituations.name: Highly anticipated movie or event cancelled
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: If plans change, everything is ruined.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: New opportunities can grow from unexpected changes.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Sharp letdown when eager anticipation meets sudden cancellation.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That disappointment is proportional to how much they cared, and that's not silly.

childhoodSituations.name: Seeing another child or animal cry or suffer
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Their pain has nothing to do with me.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Caring actions can comfort others and make a difference.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Tender sadness on behalf of someone else's pain.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That noticing others' pain is a sign of a caring heart, not a burden.

childhoodSituations.name: Excluded from a group chat
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Being left out means I don't matter.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: One group doesn't decide my value or my friendships.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Modern exclusion — watching a conversation happen without them.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That being left off one thread doesn't mean being left out of the friendship.

childhoodSituations.name: Not chosen for a special school role
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: If I'm not chosen, I'm not good enough.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: My worth isn't decided by awards or roles.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Quiet disappointment at being passed over for something they wanted.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That not being chosen this time isn't a measure of their value.

childhoodSituations.name: Last day of summer vacation / school year end
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Good things are over forever.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Every ending also brings a new beginning.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Bittersweet sadness at something good coming to a close.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That endings can be grieved and next things can still be looked forward to.

childhoodSituations.name: Looking at photos when they were 'little'
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I've lost who I used to be.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Growing changes me, but I'm still me inside.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Wistful longing for a smaller, simpler version of themselves.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That growing up doesn't erase who they were — it adds to it.

childhoodSituations.name: Intentions were good but they got in trouble anyway
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Good intentions don't matter if I make mistakes.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Honest intentions and taking responsibility both matter.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Confused hurt at being punished despite meaning well.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That intentions matter, and it's fair to explain them calmly, even after trouble.

childhoodSituations.name: Made a mistake in front of the class
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: One mistake means I'm not capable.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Mistakes are part of learning and growing.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Hot, exposed embarrassment with every eye suddenly on them.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That mistakes in public are still just mistakes, not verdicts.

childhoodSituations.name: Forgot someone's name or a social cue
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: If I forget, people won't like me.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Everyone makes mistakes, and kindness repairs them.
childhoodSituations.feeling: A flush of awkwardness at a small social slip.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That everyone forgets and fumbles sometimes — it's not a character flaw.

childhoodSituations.name: Called 'fat' or 'chubby' by a peer
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: My appearance decides my value.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: My worth comes from who I am, not how I look.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Wounded hurt at being labeled by their body.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That bodies come in every shape, and none of them need permission to take up space.

childhoodSituations.name: New glasses and feeling 'nerdy' or 'ugly'
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Looking different makes me less lovable.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: The things that make me different are part of who I am.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Self-conscious unease about looking different overnight.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That how they see feels the same, even if how they look has changed.

childhoodSituations.name: Getting acne or pimples (older kids)
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I have to look perfect to be accepted.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: My appearance doesn't define my value.
childhoodSituations.feeling: New, unfamiliar embarrassment about their changing skin.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That bodies change on their own timeline, and it says nothing about their worth.

childhoodSituations.name: Being shortest or tallest in the class line
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Being different makes me less important.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Everyone grows in their own unique way.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Awareness of standing out physically in a lineup of peers.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That height is just a number, not a ranking of anything that matters.

childhoodSituations.name: Being 'slower' at reading or math than others
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: If I learn slowly, I'm not smart.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Everyone learns at their own pace.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Quiet shame at needing more time than classmates to learn something.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That everyone's brain has its own pace, and pace isn't proof of ability.

childhoodSituations.name: Picked last for a team or called 'clumsy'
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I'm not good enough to belong.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Skills improve with practice and effort.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Sting of being ranked last, publicly, by peers.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That being picked last for one game says nothing about their overall worth.

childhoodSituations.name: Their clothes aren't as 'cool' as others'
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I need nicer things to be accepted.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Who I am matters more than what I own.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Self-conscious comparison of their clothes against everyone else's.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That style is self-expression, not a scoreboard to win.

childhoodSituations.name: Thinking 'I can't do anything right'
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I fail at everything.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I have many strengths and can keep improving.
childhoodSituations.feeling: A harsh inner voice repeating 'I can't.'
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That the inner voice can be gentler than it currently is, and that's a skill to build.

childhoodSituations.name: Sibling praised while they were ignored
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Love has to be earned by being the best.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I am loved for who I am, not because I outperform others.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Quiet hurt at being overlooked while a sibling is celebrated.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That praise for one child doesn't subtract from another's worth.

childhoodSituations.name: Project or video gets no likes or views
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: If people don't notice me, I don't matter.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: My work has value even without applause.
childhoodSituations.feeling: New-world sting of public performance with a visible scorecard.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That worth was never meant to be counted in likes.

childhoodSituations.name: Drawing doesn't look how they imagined
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: If it isn't perfect, I should stop.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Improvement comes through practice, not perfection.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Frustrated disappointment when the hand can't match the imagination yet.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That the gap between vision and skill is where all artists live, and it closes with practice.

childhoodSituations.name: Reprimanded in front of friends or guests
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Public mistakes make me less worthy.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: One embarrassing moment doesn't change my worth.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Doubled embarrassment — being corrected and watched at the same time.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That being corrected in front of others still doesn't make them any less loved.

childhoodSituations.name: Stuttered or forgot lines in a play
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: If I mess up, everyone will remember forever.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Courage is continuing even after mistakes.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Panic-laced embarrassment at forgetting words in front of everyone.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That forgetting a line isn't the same as failing — recovering it is the real skill.

childhoodSituations.name: Told their work is 'messy' or unreadable
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: If my work isn't perfect, I'm not capable.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Skills improve with practice and feedback.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Quiet shame about work that feels judged as sloppy.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That neat and good are different things, and effort shows in more than tidiness.

childhoodSituations.name: Why can't you be more like [cousin/friend]?
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I have to be like someone else to be valued.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: My unique strengths make me valuable.
childhoodSituations.feeling: The ache of being held up against someone else, and coming up short.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That comparisons say more about the comparer than the child being measured.

childhoodSituations.name: Feeling like a burden to parents
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I make life harder for everyone.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I am loved because I am part of the family, not because I'm perfect.
childhoodSituations.feeling: A heavy, private worry that they cost more than they give.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That children are never a burden — needing care is what childhood is for.

childhoodSituations.name: Feeling like they're not seen or valued
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Nobody notices or values me.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I matter even when others are busy or distracted.
childhoodSituations.feeling: A lonely feeling of going unnoticed even while present.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That being quiet doesn't mean being unimportant, and quiet needs can be spoken.

childhoodSituations.name: Secretly thinking 'I am just a bad kid'
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I am a bad person because I make mistakes.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I make mistakes, but I am still a good person who can grow.
childhoodSituations.feeling: A frightening, secret belief that they are fundamentally bad.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That behavior and identity are different — a hard moment doesn't make a hard heart.

childhoodSituations.name: Parent praises sibling's work but not theirs
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Praise decides my value.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: My worth isn't measured by comparison or praise.
childhoodSituations.feeling: A pang of hurt watching praise go somewhere else.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That there's enough praise to go around, even if it doesn't always feel that way.

childhoodSituations.name: Best friend is playing with someone else
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I'll be replaced.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Friendships grow and there's room for many connections.
childhoodSituations.feeling: The ache of being replaced, even temporarily, by someone else's company.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That friendships can include more than one person without anyone losing their place.

childhoodSituations.name: Friend got the newest toy, phone or iPad
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I need what others have to be happy.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Gratitude brings more joy than comparison.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Sharp wanting at seeing someone else get the newer, shinier thing.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That having less right now doesn't mean having less worth.

childhoodSituations.name: Classmate won Student of the Month
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Someone else's success means I'm not successful.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can celebrate others while continuing my own journey.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Competitive sting at someone else's recognition.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That someone else's win doesn't take anything away from their own effort.

childhoodSituations.name: Someone else always gets to go first
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Fair means I should get an equal turn every time.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Fairness includes patience and considering everyone.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Low-grade resentment at always being second in line.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That turns come around, even when the wait feels unfair in the moment.

childhoodSituations.name: Parent on work call when child wants to share something
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: If I have to wait, what I want to say isn't important.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: My thoughts matter, and I can wait for the right moment.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Frustrated longing to be heard right now, not later.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That waiting for attention is hard, and their voice still matters when it comes.

childhoodSituations.name: At a party but wanting the birthday gifts
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I'll only be happy if I get what someone else has.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Celebrating others can bring joy too.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Wistful envy at gifts meant for someone else.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That celebrating others can feel good too, even while wanting something similar.

childhoodSituations.name: Friend is naturally better at football or dance
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Talent is something you either have or don't.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Practice helps me improve my own abilities.
childhoodSituations.feeling: A twinge of inadequacy next to someone else's natural talent.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That other people's skill isn't a measure of their own potential.

childhoodSituations.name: New sibling gets all the attention and new things
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: The new baby has replaced me.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Love grows; it isn't divided.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Complicated jealousy toward someone who can't even talk yet.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That love expands for new arrivals — it doesn't get divided up and shrink.

childhoodSituations.name: Another kid always gets teacher's favour
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: If someone else is chosen, I'm less important.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can focus on my own growth instead of comparison.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Resentment at a favoritism that feels impossible to earn.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That one adult's favor isn't the only kind of approval worth having.

childhoodSituations.name: Friend has more followers or game skins
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Having more things or popularity makes someone better.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Real happiness and friendship can't be measured by possessions or popularity.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Comparison-driven envy fed by numbers on a screen.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That connection in real life outweighs any number online.

childhoodSituations.name: Friend went on a fancy international vacation
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Exciting experiences make someone more important.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Meaningful memories can be created anywhere.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Envy at a life that looks more exciting from the outside.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That every family's story is different, and different isn't worse.

childhoodSituations.name: Wishing they had someone else's hair or height
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I have to look different to be enough.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: My uniqueness is part of what makes me special.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Wishing to look like someone else instead of themselves.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That the features they have are the ones worth learning to love.

childhoodSituations.name: Wanting what's in a friend's lunchbox
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: What others have is always better.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Gratitude helps me enjoy what I already have.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Simple, physical envy over someone else's snack.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That trading and sharing can turn envy into connection.

childhoodSituations.name: Friend has a later bedtime or more freedom
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Different rules mean my parents are unfair.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Every family makes choices based on different needs.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Chafing against rules that feel stricter than a friend's.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That every family sets its own rules for its own good reasons.

childhoodSituations.name: Always wearing older sibling's old clothes
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: New things make someone more valuable.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: My value isn't determined by what I own.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Quiet embarrassment about wearing what's already been worn.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That hand-me-downs carry history, not less value.

childhoodSituations.name: Post-party or festival hyperactivity
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I have to follow every exciting feeling.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can enjoy excitement and still calm my body afterwards.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Buzzing, uncontainable energy with no clear place to go.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That big energy needs a big outlet, not a lecture.

childhoodSituations.name: Zoning out after too much YouTube or gaming
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: My attention controls me.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can guide my attention back to what matters.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Foggy, disconnected zoning-out after too much screen stimulation.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That the brain needs quiet time to reset after bright, fast input.

childhoodSituations.name: Noisy, overcrowded mall or festival environment
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I can't cope when everything feels overwhelming.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can notice what I need and find calm even in busy places.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Sensory flooding from noise and crowds pressing in on all sides.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That it's okay to need a quiet corner in a loud world.

childhoodSituations.name: Too many classes — tuition, sport, music all in one day
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I have to do everything perfectly.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can do my best while caring for my energy.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Frayed, thin patience from a day with no breathing room.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That rest is productive too, not just the things on the schedule.

childhoodSituations.name: Long wait at doctor, bank, or during travel
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Waiting is pointless and unbearable.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can use waiting time calmly and wisely.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Restless irritability from time stretching with nothing to do.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That boredom can be sat with — it isn't an emergency to fix.

childhoodSituations.name: Stuck indoors on a rainy day with nothing to do
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Fun only happens when things go as planned.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can create joy wherever I am.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Antsy frustration at being stuck with no outlet for the day's energy.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That indoor days can still hold adventure, just a smaller-scale one.

childhoodSituations.name: End of a long school week — brain feels full
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I should always keep going.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Rest is part of learning and growing.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Depleted, foggy exhaustion by the end of a long week.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That a full brain deserves rest, the same way a full day deserves sleep.

childhoodSituations.name: Cranky after a late night or bad sleep
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Being tired gives me no control over my behaviour.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can notice my feelings and choose kind actions.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Thin-skinned crankiness from a body running on too little sleep.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That crankiness isn't a character flaw — it's a body asking for rest.

childhoodSituations.name: Trying to do homework while TV is on
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I can't focus when there are distractions.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can gently bring my attention back.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Scattered frustration trying to focus with noise pulling attention away.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That focus needs a quiet space, and asking for one is a smart move, not a weakness.

childhoodSituations.name: Too many options for a toy or treat
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: More choices always make me happier.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Wise choices matter more than having everything.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Frozen overwhelm faced with too many options at once.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That fewer choices, offered kindly, can feel like relief instead of restriction.

childhoodSituations.name: Pressure to always 'be good' and behave
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I have to be perfect to be loved.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I am loved even while I'm learning and growing.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Quiet exhaustion from trying to be 'good' all the time.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That needing a break from being perfect is normal, not naughty.

childhoodSituations.name: Waiting for a turn on the swings
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I should always go first.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Everyone deserves a turn.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Impatient fidgeting while watching someone else get a turn.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That waiting is a skill, and it gets easier with practice, not willpower alone.

childhoodSituations.name: Switching from fun activity to chores or homework
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I should only do what I enjoy.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Responsibility helps me earn greater freedom.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Resistant friction switching from something fun to something necessary.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That transitions go smoother with a warning and a moment to finish up.

childhoodSituations.name: The 'before dinner' energy crash
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: My feelings should decide my behaviour.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can care for my feelings without hurting others.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Sudden, sharp crankiness as hunger outruns patience.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That hunger changes mood, and naming it early heads off a meltdown.

childhoodSituations.name: Uncomfortable uniform, flickering lights, strong smells
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I can't cope when things feel uncomfortable.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can care for myself and ask for help when needed.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Irritable overload from textures, lights, or smells that feel like too much.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That sensory needs are real needs, not fussiness.

childhoodSituations.name: Waiting very excitedly for birthday or special package
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Waiting ruins the fun.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Anticipation can make joyful moments even sweeter.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Electric, can't-sit-still excitement that's hard to contain.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That excitement is welcome, even when it needs a little channeling.

childhoodSituations.name: Trying to learn a very hard new concept or language
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: If I don't understand quickly, I'm not smart.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Understanding grows with patience and practice.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Mental strain from a concept that isn't clicking yet.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That confusion is the first step of learning, not a sign of failure.

childhoodSituations.name: Moving to a new home or city
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I'll never feel at home again.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Home grows wherever love and connection grow.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Unmooring uncertainty about leaving everything familiar behind.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That home is made of people first, walls second.

childhoodSituations.name: Moving abroad (very relevant for NRI families)
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I won't belong in a new country.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can build new friendships while keeping my roots.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Disorientation layered with the extra weight of a whole new culture.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That belonging can grow in more than one place at once.

childhoodSituations.name: Parents separating or getting a divorce
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: My family is broken and I'm not safe anymore.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Love and security can continue even when families change.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Confused grief about a family shape that's about to change.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That both parents' love continues, even when the household doesn't stay the same.

childhoodSituations.name: A parent starts a new job with different hours
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Less time together means less love.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Love isn't measured by time but by care and connection.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Uneasy adjustment to a parent being less available than before.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That love isn't measured only in hours in the room.

childhoodSituations.name: Starting at a completely new school
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Nobody will accept me.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can create new friendships by being myself.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Anxious blankness facing a place with no familiar faces yet.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That every new place becomes familiar with enough small, repeated days.

childhoodSituations.name: Favourite teacher changes mid-year
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Good things never last.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: New people can also become trusted guides.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Quiet grief for a favorite adult who is no longer in charge.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That good people can still be missed even after they're gone from a role.

childhoodSituations.name: Sudden cancellation of a normal routine event
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Everything has to happen the way I expected.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can adapt and discover new possibilities.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Frustrated disorientation when something ordinary suddenly doesn't happen.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That flexibility is a muscle, and disappointment can be worked through, not avoided.

childhoodSituations.name: Summer ending and school starting again
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Fun is over now.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Every new season brings new adventures.
childhoodSituations.feeling: A wistful, unsettled feeling as one familiar season hands off to another.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That endings and beginnings are the same event seen from two sides.

childhoodSituations.name: Growing pains, first tooth loss, puberty signs
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Growing and changing is scary.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Growing is a natural and wonderful part of life.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Confusing physical sensations that don't match how they feel inside.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That growing bodies are strange and normal at the same time.

childhoodSituations.name: Friend suddenly acting different or 'cooler'
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I have to change to keep my friends.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Real friendships accept me for who I am.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Uneasy watchfulness as a friendship starts to feel different.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That friends can change without the friendship having to end.

childhoodSituations.name: Game or app changes interface completely
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I don't like change, so I can't enjoy it.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can learn new ways of doing things.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Mild disorientation at a familiar tool suddenly behaving differently.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That adapting to change is a skill, practiced on small things first.

childhoodSituations.name: New nanny or household helper joins family
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: New people can't become part of my safe world.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Trust grows through kindness and shared experiences.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Wary uncertainty about a new person joining the household routine.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That trust with a new person builds the same way it did with the old one — slowly.

childhoodSituations.name: News of an upcoming surgery or treatment
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I won't be able to handle what's coming.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can face difficult moments one brave step at a time.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Quiet fear behind news of an upcoming medical event.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That worry and information can sit side by side, and questions are always welcome.

childhoodSituations.name: Family having to cut back on treats or outings
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Happiness comes from having more.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Love, togetherness and gratitude bring lasting happiness.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Confused disappointment at hearing 'we can't this time.'
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That family resources ebb and flow, and love isn't rationed the same way money is.

childhoodSituations.name: Waiting anxiously for exam results
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: My marks decide my value.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: My effort and character matter more than any score.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Stomach-churning anticipation while waiting for news out of their control.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That the waiting is often harder than the result, and both can be survived.

childhoodSituations.name: First time staying overnight away from home
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I can't feel safe away from home.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can feel safe in new places with trusted people.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Nervous excitement tangled with homesickness before a first night away.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That being brave doesn't mean not missing home — both can be true at once.

childhoodSituations.name: Stopping a favourite hobby or activity
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: If one chapter ends, all the joy is gone.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: New interests and opportunities will come.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Quiet grief for a hobby or identity that's ending.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That interests can change without erasing what was loved about the old one.

childhoodSituations.name: Overheard adults talk about 'a big change coming'
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Unknown changes are always bad.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can face change calmly and ask questions when I'm unsure.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Anxious eavesdropping-driven dread about an unnamed 'big change.'
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That asking directly is safer than imagining, and most answers are less scary than the unknown.

childhoodSituations.name: Told a lie to a parent and feels a 'heavy' stomach
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Hiding the truth will protect me.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Honesty brings trust, even after mistakes.
childhoodSituations.feeling: A heavy, guilty knot in the stomach after bending the truth.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That honesty feels lighter than the lie, even when it's harder to say.

childhoodSituations.name: Friends asked them to steal or break a rule
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I must follow my friends to belong.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Doing what's right is more important than fitting in.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Torn unease between wanting to belong and knowing something is wrong.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That real friends don't require doing something that feels wrong.

childhoodSituations.name: Watched someone get bullied and did nothing
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Speaking up won't make a difference.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Small acts of courage can protect others.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Guilty discomfort at having stood by while someone else got hurt.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That speaking up, even quietly to a trusted adult, is its own kind of courage.

childhoodSituations.name: A mean kid got praised or rewarded
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Bad behaviour always wins.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can't control others, but I can choose my own values.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Confused indignation when good behavior isn't the one that gets rewarded.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That doing right doesn't depend on being noticed for it.

childhoodSituations.name: Wants to play but knows they should study
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I should always do what feels fun now.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Choosing responsibility today helps me tomorrow.
childhoodSituations.feeling: An inner tug-of-war between what's fun and what's responsible.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That choosing the harder, better thing gets easier with practice, not willpower alone.

childhoodSituations.name: Tempted to look at friend's paper during a test
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Cheating is okay if it helps me succeed.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Honest effort builds real confidence.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Tempting shortcut-thinking under the pressure of a ticking clock.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That their own effort, even if smaller, belongs to them in a way a copied answer never will.

childhoodSituations.name: Told a 'bad' secret they feel should be shared
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Keeping every secret makes me a good friend.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Safe adults should know secrets that can protect someone.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Uneasy custodianship of information that feels too big to hold alone.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That some secrets are meant to be shared with a trusted adult, and that's not betrayal.

childhoodSituations.name: Broke something by mistake and hid it
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Hiding mistakes makes them disappear.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Taking responsibility helps rebuild trust.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Panicked guilt after damage they're afraid to admit to.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That owning a mistake quickly is easier than carrying the secret of it.

childhoodSituations.name: Realised some kids don't have food or shoes
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Other people's struggles have nothing to do with me.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Kindness and generosity can make a real difference.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Unsettled awareness of unfairness bigger than their own life.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That noticing unfairness in the world is the first step toward caring about it.

childhoodSituations.name: Saw a parent or teacher break a rule they enforce
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Rules only matter when they're convenient.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can choose integrity regardless of what others do.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Confusing cognitive dissonance seeing a rule-enforcer break their own rule.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That adults are still learning too, and noticing that is a sign of a sharp, fair mind.

childhoodSituations.name: Someone online asked for their personal password
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Everyone online can be trusted.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I protect myself by making safe choices and asking trusted adults.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Wary unease at a request that feels like it's crossing a line.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That trusted adults, not strangers online, are who private information belongs to.

childhoodSituations.name: Saw someone litter and felt upset but said nothing
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: One person's actions don't matter.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Small responsible actions help care for our world.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Frustrated helplessness witnessing carelessness they can't undo.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That one person's small action, repeated, adds up to real care for a shared place.

childhoodSituations.name: Saw a stray animal being treated badly
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: It's not my place to help.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Every living being deserves kindness and care.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Distressed empathy at cruelty toward a creature who can't speak up.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That kindness to animals is a rehearsal for kindness everywhere.

childhoodSituations.name: Failed to keep a promise they made to a friend
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: One broken promise means the friendship is ruined.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Trust can be rebuilt through honesty and consistent actions.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Guilty regret at letting a friend down.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That a broken promise can be repaired with an honest apology and a next try.

childhoodSituations.name: Feels guilty for not including someone in play
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: There's only room for some people.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Everyone deserves a chance to belong.
childhoodSituations.feeling: A tender guilt about a small social exclusion.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That noticing the discomfort of leaving someone out is the beginning of including them next time.

childhoodSituations.name: Friend said something mean about their culture or family
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I should hide who I am to fit in.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: My identity deserves respect, and I can respect others too.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Defensive hurt layered with confusion after an identity-based jab.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That their family's traditions are not something to be embarrassed by — curiosity from others is a chance to teach, not a verdict.

childhoodSituations.name: Found something and doesn't know whether to keep it
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: If I found it, it belongs to me.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Doing the right thing matters more than getting something extra.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Uncertain hesitation weighing honesty against a lucky find.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That doing the effortful right thing (asking, returning) feels better in the long run than keeping something unclaimed.

childhoodSituations.name: Overheard talk about politics, protests, or injustice
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: The world is only unfair and nothing can change.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Fairness grows through understanding, courage and responsible action.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Confused unease absorbing adult-sized topics without adult-sized context.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That the world has hard chapters and repair, and it's alright to ask questions about both.

childhoodSituations.name: Best friend makes a new best friend
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: If my friend likes someone else, I'll be forgotten.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Friendships can grow without replacing each other.
childhoodSituations.feeling: A sharp pang of replacement — like their special spot just got taken.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That love and friendship expand to fit more people, they don't get divided up.

childhoodSituations.name: Friends don't reply to messages
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: No reply means they don't care about me.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I shouldn't assume the worst before I know the truth.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Anxious spiraling, assuming the worst from silence.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That a slow reply is rarely a verdict, and checking in beats assuming.

childhoodSituations.name: Accidentally left out of a game
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Being left out means I don't belong.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can help create spaces where everyone belongs.
childhoodSituations.feeling: A quiet sting of exclusion, even without anyone meaning it.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That noticing who's left out, even by accident, is worth speaking up about.

childhoodSituations.name: A secret wasn't shared with them
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: If I'm not told everything, I'm not important.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Trust grows through honesty, not knowing every secret.
childhoodSituations.feeling: A hurt feeling of being on the outside of something.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That not knowing everything doesn't mean being less trusted or valued.

childhoodSituations.name: Friend copies their work or idea
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: If someone copies me, I've lost what makes me special.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: My ideas and creativity remain valuable.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Territorial frustration at losing what felt uniquely theirs.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That being copied is often a compliment in disguise, and originality isn't used up by sharing.

childhoodSituations.name: A friend wins while they lose
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Someone else's success makes me less successful.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can celebrate others while continuing my own journey.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Competitive sting swallowed under a forced smile.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That someone else's win and their own effort can both be true at once.

childhoodSituations.name: Friend breaks a promise
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Once trust is broken, it can never be repaired.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Honest conversations and actions can rebuild trust.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Disappointment curdling into distrust.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That one broken promise is a repair conversation, not proof the friendship is over.

childhoodSituations.name: Rumours or gossip spread about them
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I have to prove myself to everyone.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Truth and character matter more than rumours.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Helpless anger at a story about them they didn't get to tell.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That their actions and character speak louder than a rumor, over time.

childhoodSituations.name: Friend apologises after hurting them
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Holding on to hurt keeps me safe.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Forgiveness helps relationships heal and grow.
childhoodSituations.feeling: A tug-of-war between wanting to forgive and wanting to protect themselves.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That accepting an apology is a choice they get to make in their own time.

childhoodSituations.name: They hurt a friend's feelings by mistake
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: One mistake makes me a bad friend.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can apologise, repair and learn from my mistakes.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Guilty regret at seeing the effect of their own words.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That a sincere apology repairs more than staying quiet out of embarrassment.

childhoodSituations.name: Asked to choose between two friends
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I have to choose one person over another.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can be kind and fair to everyone.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Squeezed, torn loyalty with no comfortable answer.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That they don't have to rank people they care about.

childhoodSituations.name: Lost during a team game because of their mistake
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Everyone will blame me forever.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Mistakes are part of teamwork and learning.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Public, hot-faced guilt at letting the team down.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That one mistake in a team game is shared, not carried alone.

childhoodSituations.name: Teammate isn't doing their part
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: I have to control others for things to go well.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Cooperation grows through patience and communication.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Simmering frustration at carrying more than their share.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That naming the problem calmly works better than doing it all silently.

childhoodSituations.name: Friend gets a pet they always wanted
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Life is unfair because I don't have what they have.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: I can be genuinely happy for others while appreciating my own life.
childhoodSituations.feeling: A wistful envy dressed up as happiness for a friend.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That wanting what someone else has doesn't make their own life less good.

childhoodSituations.name: A younger child wants to join the game
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Younger children will spoil our fun.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Everyone deserves a chance to belong.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Impatient reluctance to slow down for someone less skilled.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That making room for someone smaller is its own kind of strength.

childhoodSituations.name: Friend is nervous before a performance
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: It's not my job to help.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Encouragement can help someone become brave.
childhoodSituations.feeling: A protective instinct paired with not knowing what to do with it.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That a few kind words before a hard moment can genuinely help someone else.

childhoodSituations.name: Classmate is new and sitting alone
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: Someone else will help them.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Small acts of kindness can make someone feel welcome.
childhoodSituations.feeling: A flicker of concern quickly talked out of by shyness.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That the small effort of saying hello can change someone's whole day.

childhoodSituations.name: Friend keeps interrupting while talking
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: The loudest person should be heard.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Listening is an important way to show respect.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Mounting frustration at not getting to finish a thought.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That asking to be heard, calmly, is fair and normal.

childhoodSituations.name: Group project where everyone has different ideas
childhoodSituations.falseBelief: My idea has to be chosen.
childhoodSituations.trueBelief: Great ideas grow when people work together.
childhoodSituations.feeling: Frustrated insistence that their idea is the right one.
childhoodSituations.parentTeach: That combining ideas usually makes something better than any one idea alone.

emotionalArcs.avoid: Fixing the flaw instead of accepting it.

emotionalArcs.name: 2. Circle of Safety
emotionalArcs.description: Temporary separation becomes an opportunity to build trust and reassurance.
emotionalArcs.whyItWorks: Helps children process separation anxiety safely.
emotionalArcs.avoid: Turning it into a dangerous rescue.

emotionalArcs.name: 3. Empathetic Witness
emotionalArcs.description: Healing begins when someone quietly listens instead of trying to solve the problem.

emotionalArcs.name: 4. Sensory Discovery
emotionalArcs.description: Exploring nature creates emotional growth through experience.

emotionalArcs.name: 5. Triumphant Teamwork
emotionalArcs.description: Friends combine different strengths to solve a problem together.

emotionalArcs.name: 6. Mindful De-escalation
emotionalArcs.description: A child gradually slows down until they feel calm and secure.
emotionalArcs.whyItWorks: Excellent for bedtime and emotional regulation.

emotionalArcs.name: 7. Rhythmic Growth
emotionalArcs.description: Growth happens through effort, mistakes, rest and transformation.

emotionalArcs.name: 8. Underdog's Wit
emotionalArcs.description: A small hero succeeds through intelligence instead of strength.

emotionalArcs.name: 9. Empowered Boundary
emotionalArcs.description: Holding a healthy boundary becomes a joyful achievement.

emotionalArcs.name: 10. Generous Heart
emotionalArcs.description: Sharing transforms loneliness into connection.

emotionalArcs.name: 11. Emotional Harbor
emotionalArcs.description: Big emotions are expressed safely before returning to connection.
emotionalArcs.whyItWorks: Validates anger while preserving emotional safety.

emotionalArcs.name: 12. Validated Grump
emotionalArcs.description: A terrible day becomes bearable when feelings are acknowledged.
emotionalArcs.whyItWorks: Builds resilience through validation instead of forced positivity.

emotionalArcs.name: 13. Creative Empowerment
emotionalArcs.description: A child solves a problem through imagination and creativity.
emotionalArcs.whyItWorks: Builds creative confidence instead of dependence.

emotionalArcs.name: 14. Identity Reframing
emotionalArcs.description: A child learns their difference is a unique strength.
emotionalArcs.avoid: Changing the child to fit in.

emotionalArcs.name: 15. Resourceful Improviser
emotionalArcs.description: Losing something leads to discovering an even better solution.

emotionalArcs.name: 16. Surprise Guest
emotionalArcs.description: An unexpected visitor or event enriches everyone's lives.

emotionalArcs.name: 17. Infinite Measure
emotionalArcs.description: A child discovers love cannot be measured because it keeps growing.

emotionalArcs.name: 18. Runaway Logic
emotionalArcs.description: One simple action creates an increasingly funny chain reaction.
emotionalArcs.whyItWorks: Teaches cause and effect through humour.

emotionalArcs.name: 19. Comic Pivot
emotionalArcs.description: The hero's focus suddenly changes, ending the conflict.

emotionalArcs.name: 20. Curious Insecurity
emotionalArcs.description: Questions about identity lead to deeper confidence.

emotionalArcs.name: 21. Courageous Breath
emotionalArcs.description: A child calms themselves before facing a challenge.
emotionalArcs.whyItWorks: Teaches emotional regulation in stressful moments.

emotionalArcs.name: 22. Appreciated Helper
emotionalArcs.description: A helpful child realizes their kindness is seen and valued.

emotionalArcs.name: 23. Melodramatic Threat
emotionalArcs.description: Dramatic reactions soften through understanding and reassurance.
emotionalArcs.whyItWorks: Lets children laugh at exaggerated emotions.

emotionalArcs.name: 24. Silent Awe
emotionalArcs.description: A child quietly experiences something beautiful without needing words.
