openings.name: The Vulnerable Wanderer
openings.description: Introduce the hero facing a relatable emotional challenge before the adventure begins.
openings.howItWorks: Starts with emotion before action so children immediately identify with the hero.
openings.whyItWorks: Empathy is created before curiosity, making readers care about what happens next.
openings.openingFormula: Child struggling → Small glimpse of world → Something unexpected appears
openings.illustrationGoal: Show the hero small within a rich environment, with body language revealing the emotional state.
openings.writingTips: Keep the challenge small and relatable. Show emotion through actions instead of explaining it.

openings.name: The Tiny Mystery
openings.description: Begin with a small unexplained event that sparks curiosity.
openings.howItWorks: Gives the child an immediate question to solve.
openings.openingFormula: Normal world → Strange detail appears → Hero decides to investigate
openings.illustrationGoal: Highlight one unusual object or event while keeping the rest of the scene ordinary.
openings.writingTips: Mystery should be small enough for children to understand but intriguing enough to continue reading.

openings.name: The Unexpected Interruption
openings.description: The hero's ordinary day is suddenly interrupted by an unexpected event.
openings.howItWorks: Quickly shifts from normal life into adventure.
openings.whyItWorks: Creates momentum immediately without long setup.
openings.openingFormula: Normal day → Unexpected interruption → Hero reacts
openings.illustrationGoal: Contrast peaceful routine with sudden movement or change.
openings.writingTips: Keep the interruption simple and easy to understand. The hero should react immediately.

openings.name: The Everyday Wonder
openings.description: Begin in an ordinary place where something beautiful or unusual is quietly discovered.
openings.howItWorks: Invites children to notice wonder in familiar surroundings.
openings.whyItWorks: Builds curiosity through observation instead of action.
openings.openingFormula: Ordinary place → Tiny beautiful detail → Hero notices something different
openings.illustrationGoal: Rich environmental illustration with one subtle magical or surprising detail.
openings.writingTips: Let the illustration do much of the storytelling. Keep text gentle and minimal.

openings.name: The Emotional Spark
openings.description: Open with a strong feeling or emotional problem the hero is experiencing.
openings.howItWorks: Emotion becomes the story's starting point rather than the plot.
openings.openingFormula: Strong emotion → Small situation showing it → Something changes
openings.illustrationGoal: Close-up of facial expression and body language.
openings.writingTips: Show emotion through behaviour rather than naming it.

openings.name: The Invitation
openings.description: Someone invites the hero to help, join or explore something new.
openings.howItWorks: Gives the story a clear purpose from the beginning.
openings.openingFormula: Invitation arrives → Hero hesitates → Accepts the invitation
openings.illustrationGoal: Show two characters interacting with excitement or curiosity.
openings.writingTips: The invitation should feel exciting but believable.

openings.name: The Missing Something
openings.description: An important object, person or idea has disappeared.
openings.whyItWorks: Children immediately understand what needs to be solved.
openings.openingFormula: Something important is missing → Hero discovers it → Search begins
openings.illustrationGoal: Empty space where something should be.
openings.writingTips: Make the missing item emotionally meaningful.

openings.name: The Promise
openings.description: The hero makes—or receives—a meaningful promise.
openings.whyItWorks: Readers want to know whether the promise will be kept.
openings.openingFormula: Promise made → Responsibility accepted → Challenge begins
openings.illustrationGoal: Warm interaction between characters that shows the relationship.
openings.writingTips: Keep the promise simple and emotionally important.

openings.name: The Race Against Time
openings.description: The hero must complete something before a deadline.
openings.howItWorks: Introduces urgency from the very first page.
openings.openingFormula: Deadline introduced → Stakes explained → Hero decides to act
openings.illustrationGoal: Show a visible countdown (setting sun, approaching storm, festival preparations, etc.).
openings.writingTips: Make the deadline easy for children to understand and emotionally meaningful.

openings.name: The Impossible Task
openings.description: The hero is asked to do something that feels far beyond their ability.
openings.whyItWorks: Children instantly root for an underdog.
openings.openingFormula: Impossible challenge → Hero doubts themselves → First small attempt
openings.illustrationGoal: Show the huge challenge compared to the small hero.
openings.writingTips: Make the task appear impossible—but secretly achievable through growth.

endings.name: The Circular Return
endings.description: The story ends where it began, but the hero has changed.
endings.howItWorks: Mirrors the opening to highlight growth.
endings.whyItWorks: Children enjoy recognizing familiar scenes with new meaning.
endings.endingFormula: Return to opening → Show changed behaviour → Quiet emotional close
endings.replayTrigger: Opening scene echoes with new meaning
endings.illustrationGoal: Same location as the opening, but brighter and more alive
endings.writingTips: Let actions reveal the change instead of explaining it.

endings.name: The Quiet Internal Victory
endings.description: The biggest success is emotional rather than external.
endings.howItWorks: The mission matters, but the hero's inner change matters more.
endings.endingFormula: Mission completed → Hero thinks differently → Peaceful ending
endings.replayTrigger: Small visual callback to the emotional journey
endings.illustrationGoal: Calm close-up of the hero showing confidence
endings.writingTips: Show the emotional change through behaviour and expression.

endings.name: The Ripple Effect
endings.description: The hero's change positively influences others.
endings.howItWorks: Shows that personal growth spreads outward.
endings.endingFormula: Hero changes → Others respond → Community benefits
endings.writingTips: Keep the focus on influence, not praise.

endings.name: The Gentle Surprise
endings.description: A small unexpected reveal adds delight without changing the story.
endings.whyItWorks: Creates an "Aha!" moment and encourages rereading.
endings.endingFormula: Problem solved → Small hidden reveal → Smile
endings.replayTrigger: Hidden clue that makes earlier pages more meaningful
endings.illustrationGoal: Focus on one surprising visual detail
endings.writingTips: Keep the surprise small and believable.

endings.name: The New Beginning
endings.description: The adventure ends by opening a hopeful next chapter.
endings.howItWorks: Gives closure while suggesting future possibilities.
endings.whyItWorks: Makes the story world feel alive beyond the final page.
endings.endingFormula: Mission complete → New opportunity appears → Hopeful close
endings.replayTrigger: Small hint of the next adventure
endings.illustrationGoal: Hero looking toward a new horizon
endings.writingTips: End one story completely before hinting at another.

endings.name: The Shared Celebration
endings.description: Friends, family or the community celebrate together.
endings.howItWorks: Rewards the journey with shared joy.
endings.illustrationGoal: Rich festive spread full of life
endings.writingTips: Keep the celebration connected to the emotional journey.

endings.name: The Passing Forward
endings.description: The hero shares the wisdom, kindness or courage they discovered with someone else.
endings.howItWorks: The transformation is completed by helping another character.
endings.whyItWorks: Shows that true growth naturally spreads to others.
endings.endingFormula: Hero transforms → Helps another → Wisdom continues
endings.replayTrigger: A younger or struggling character now begins their own journey.
endings.illustrationGoal: Hero helping another in a scene similar to the one where they once needed help.
endings.writingTips: Show the wisdom through actions, not speeches.

endings.name: Nature Responds
endings.description: Nature quietly reflects the hero's emotional transformation.
endings.howItWorks: The environment changes to mirror the emotional resolution.
endings.whyItWorks: Creates a memorable visual ending without explaining the lesson.
endings.endingFormula: Hero changes → Nature responds → Quiet final image
endings.replayTrigger: Readers notice nature behaving differently on a reread.
endings.illustrationGoal: Blooming flowers, returning birds, sunlight breaking through clouds, calm river.
endings.writingTips: Keep the change subtle and symbolic.

endings.name: The Callback
endings.description: The ending echoes a moment, line or image from the opening, but with new emotional meaning.
endings.howItWorks: Creates symmetry and highlights the hero's transformation.
endings.whyItWorks: Children enjoy recognising familiar moments with a deeper understanding.
endings.endingFormula: Repeat opening moment → Hero responds differently → Quiet close
endings.replayTrigger: Children notice how the opening and ending mirror each other.
endings.illustrationGoal: Nearly identical composition to the opening illustration, but with changed body language and surroundings.
endings.writingTips: Use visual storytelling more than dialogue.

endings.name: The Open Door
endings.description: The main story feels complete while gently hinting that more adventures are possible.
endings.howItWorks: Provides closure while expanding the world.
endings.endingFormula: Mission complete → Small mystery remains → Hopeful final image
endings.replayTrigger: A tiny unexplored path, unopened letter, distant light, new map or new friend appears.
endings.illustrationGoal: Hero looking toward a new horizon or discovering one last tiny clue.
endings.writingTips: The current emotional journey must feel complete before teasing the future.
